content.value_statement: End-to-end tests often fail because selectors, waits, and configuration are inconsistent. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Playwright patterns for reliable browser tests.
actual_capabilities: Guides Playwright configuration for projects, browsers, reporters, retries, traces, and web server setup.
Recommends resilient locators using roles, labels, text, filters, and test IDs when needed.
Explains page object patterns, fixtures, authentication storage state, and test isolation.
Shows network mocking, API error simulation, and request header modification for stable tests.
Guides debugging with Playwright Inspector, traces, screenshots, and UI mode.
Adds accessibility and visual regression testing examples using common Playwright integrations.
limitations: Does not execute tests unless the assistant chooses to run external commands.
Does not replace application-specific test data, credentials, or environment setup.
Examples assume modern Playwright versions and TypeScript-oriented projects.
Cannot guarantee selectors without access to rendered application markup.

use_cases.title: Create E2E Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Design browser tests for forms, authentication flows, tables, dashboards, and error states using Playwright best practices.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Flaky Tests
use_cases.description: Replace brittle selectors, fixed waits, and unclear assertions with resilient locators and auto-waiting expectations.

use_cases.title: Improve CI Test Runs
use_cases.description: Tune retries, workers, traces, screenshots, reports, and browser projects for reliable continuous integration runs.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Playwright test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Playwright test plan for this user flow. Include key assertions, locator strategy, and setup requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Locators
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of selectors and assertions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Playwright tests for brittle selectors and weak assertions. Suggest safer role, label, or filter-based alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Page Objects
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced structure for reusable test code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Playwright suite into page objects and fixtures. Keep tests readable and preserve test isolation.

prompt_templates.title: Design CI Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced test reliability and pipeline planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Playwright CI strategy for this project. Cover browsers, retries, workers, trace capture, reports, and artifact handling.

output_examples.input: Create a Playwright test plan for a login flow.
output_examples.output: A structured plan covering successful login, invalid credentials, required fields, authenticated redirects, and trace capture for failed runs.
A focused review that replaces brittle selectors, removes fixed waits, adds stable readiness checks, and isolates network dependencies.

output_examples.input: Add accessibility testing to an existing suite.
output_examples.output: A practical approach for accessibility scans, scoped checks, violation reporting, and CI-friendly failure handling.

best_practices: Prefer role and label locators before CSS selectors or test IDs.
Use auto-waiting assertions and specific readiness signals instead of fixed sleeps.
Keep authentication state and fixtures isolated from production accounts and secrets.
anti_patterns: Using brittle CSS chains when accessible locators are available.
Depending on network idle for pages with ongoing background traffic.
Running generated tests against production accounts or real payment flows.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design, debug, and maintain Playwright browser tests using practical patterns and examples.

faq.question: Can it create page objects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for page object classes, fixtures, navigation methods, and reusable assertions.

faq.question: Does it support API and network testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers request routing, mocked responses, API errors, slow responses, and request header changes.

faq.question: Can it help with flaky tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends resilient locators, auto-waiting assertions, better readiness checks, and improved test isolation.

faq.question: Does it run Playwright commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Any command execution depends on the host assistant workflow.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
